# Draft:Swami Jitendra Tiwari

----
Swami Jitendra Tiwari
Swami Jitendra Tiwari (born 10 July 1976) is an Indian spiritual leader, social worker, and cultural activist known for his contributions to Sanatan Dharma, animal welfare, humanitarian service, and rural development. He is associated with several religious, charitable, and cooperative institutions in India, particularly in the states of Uttar Pradesh and Karnataka.
He is the founder and head of multiple spiritual and social organizations, including Shiv Ganga Dham, Shivganga Jeev Jantu Kalyan Ashram, and Shri Hanuman Sena. His work focuses on spiritual practice, promotion of traditional Indian culture, public welfare, environmental conservation, and relief activities during natural disasters and public emergencies.
Early Life & Spiritual Journey
Jitendra Tiwari Swami Ji was born on 10 July 1976 in Uttar Pradesh, India. Under the guidance of his spiritual mentor, he began spiritual discipline and ascetic practices at the age of 14. At an early stage of his life, he undertook prolonged meditation and penance, which later became central to his spiritual identity.
From 1999 onward, he adopted a strict ascetic lifestyle, renouncing cooked and grain-based food and sustaining himself only on fruits and milk for nearly fourteen years. In 2000, he performed intense spiritual practices at major Hindu pilgrimage sites, including Haridwar, Kedarnath, and Rameshwaram, where he is reported to have undertaken standing meditation in flowing water for extended periods.
Philosophy
Swami Ji advocates a philosophy centered on service to humanity, compassion toward all living beings, social equality, and harmonious coexistence with nature. He emphasizes respect for all religions, castes, and spiritual paths and promotes a disciplined, ethical way of life rooted in traditional Indian values.
Religious and Cultural Activities
Swami Ji has been actively involved in the promotion of Sanatan Dharma and traditional Indian spiritual values.
In 2004, he established religious and cultural institutions in Bengaluru, including Shivganga Ashram and Shivganga Dham, aimed at spreading spiritual awareness and cultural education.
In 2006, he organized large-scale religious ceremonies such as the Navchandi Mahayagya and Ramcharitmanas Mahayagya in association with Saint Vidya Das Baba.
]]
Between 2008 and 2014, he played a key role in the development of religious infrastructure at Kishkindha, a site traditionally believed to be associated with the birthplace of Lord Hanuman. Activities included the construction of Shri Ramanuj Dev Pathshala, organization of cultural programs, and development works carried out through public participation and charitable trusts.
Social Service and Humanitarian Work
Jitendra Tiwari Swami Ji has been involved in social welfare initiatives for over two decades.
From 2000 to 2022, he supported rural water conservation efforts, including the construction and renovation of ponds and wells in several districts of Uttar Pradesh. He has also facilitated the installation of hand pumps for economically disadvantaged families in Karnataka.
During the COVID-19 pandemic (2020–2021), he coordinated relief efforts for migrant workers and affected communities in Karnataka and Uttar Pradesh, providing food, drinking water, masks, sanitizers, and other essential supplies.
He has additionally supported educational and healthcare needs of children from underprivileged backgrounds.
Organizational Roles
* Has been Member Zonal Railway Users Consultative Committee (ZRUCC)
* Founder and Chairman, Shiv Ganga Credit Cooperative Limited
* President, Shiv Ganga Jeev Jantu Kalyan Ashram, Pratapgarh, Uttar Pradesh
* Founder and Chairman, Shiv Ganga Dham, Bengaluru
* Founder, Shiv Ganga Associates, Bengaluru
* Head, Shiv Bajrang Dham Ashram, Uttar Pradesh
* National President, Shri Hanuman Sena
Education and Languages
* Education: Sanskrit and Astrology (Jyotish)
* Languages: Hindi, Kannada, English
